bench_angle.label: Non-uniform excitation of pec major, flat vs inclined bench (EMG)

rom_review.label: Kassiano 2023 review: range of motion & hypertrophy (muscles like quads, biceps, triceps favour long lengths)

delt_emg.label: EMG of deltoids across bench, fly, press, lateral raise

triceps_oh.label: Maeo 2022: overhead vs neutral arm triceps training (MRI, 12 wk)

biceps_preacher.label: Preacher vs Bayesian curl: similar growth (2025)

ham_curl.label: Maeo 2021: seated vs prone leg curl hamstring growth

glute_squat.label: Plotkin 2023: hip thrust vs back squat, glute & thigh growth

calf_rom.label: Kassiano 2023: calf raises at long muscle lengths

load_meta.label: Schoenfeld 2017 meta-analysis: low- vs high-load training (21 studies; heavier loads gave greater 1RM strength gains)

load_fiber.label: Low- vs high-load training, muscle fibre hypertrophy meta-analysis (no significant difference)

failure_meta.label: Proximity to failure and hypertrophy: systematic review with meta-analysis (no evidence that training to failure is superior)

failure_rir.label: 8-week trial: training to failure vs leaving 1-2 reps in reserve gave similar growth in resistance-trained people

volume_meta.label: Schoenfeld 2017: weekly volume dose-response (more weekly sets, more growth; unclear beyond ~10 sets per muscle)

freq_meta.label: Schoenfeld 2018: training frequency (no meaningful effect when weekly volume is equal)

exercises.name: Incline dumbbell press (~30°)
exercises.why: EMG: upper pec activation peaked around a 30° incline; flat bench favours the mid/lower fibres. EMG shows activation, not proven growth.

exercises.name: Barbell bench press
exercises.why: Consistently among the highest pec major activation in EMG comparisons; easy to load progressively.

exercises.name: Machine chest press
exercises.why: Stable and easy to train close to failure. No direct growth study found; chosen for practicality.

exercises.name: Cable fly (stretch at the bottom)
exercises.why: Loads the pec in the lengthened position; extrapolated from the muscle-length literature, not a chest-specific trial.

exercises.name: Push-up
exercises.why: Reported to match bench press activation at comparable relative load; good fallback with no equipment.

exercises.name: Lat pulldown
exercises.why: Lat EMG appears similar to pull-ups and the load is easy to adjust. Direct back-growth evidence is thin; this is a practical pick.

exercises.name: Pull-up
exercises.why: Similar lat activation to pulldowns in the studies I found; use when you can hit your rep range.

exercises.name: Chest-supported row
exercises.why: Removes lower-back fatigue as the limiter so the back works harder. Practical rationale, no direct trial found.

exercises.name: Seated cable row
exercises.why: A 2004 EMG study found a high lat-to-biceps ratio for wide-grip pulldown and seated row.

exercises.name: One-arm dumbbell row
exercises.why: Simple, unilateral, easy to progress.

exercises.name: Lateral raise (cable or dumbbell)
exercises.why: Highest medial-delt activation in an EMG comparison with presses and flys. Medial delt is the part presses train least.

exercises.name: Dumbbell shoulder press
exercises.why: Trains front delts hard and shares work with triceps; pairs with lateral raises.

exercises.name: Machine shoulder press
exercises.why: Stable, easy to take close to failure.

exercises.name: Reverse pec deck / rear-delt fly
exercises.why: Isolates the rear delt, which bench and press movements barely hit.

exercises.name: Face pull
exercises.why: Rear delt and upper back; practical rather than study-backed.

exercises.name: Incline dumbbell curl
exercises.why: Biceps stretched under load (long muscle length). Evidence is mixed: one trial favoured long-length curls, a 2025 trial found preacher and Bayesian curls similar.

exercises.name: Preacher curl
exercises.equip: EZ bar or dumbbell, preacher bench
exercises.why: Compared head to head with Bayesian curls: similar growth.

exercises.name: Bayesian cable curl
exercises.why: Arm behind the body, biceps stretched; similar growth to preacher curls in a 2025 trial.

exercises.name: EZ-bar curl
exercises.why: Easy to progress heavy; the standard fallback.

exercises.name: Hammer curl
exercises.why: Hits brachialis and brachioradialis too; practical, no direct trial found.

exercises.name: Overhead cable triceps extension
exercises.why: In a 12-week MRI study the overhead arm position grew the long head ~28.5% vs ~19.6% for the neutral position, with the other heads also favouring overhead.

exercises.name: Overhead dumbbell extension
exercises.why: Same overhead position as the study without needing a cable; the study itself used cable extensions.

exercises.name: Cable pushdown
exercises.why: This is the neutral-arm comparator in the study: it works, just grew the long head less.

exercises.name: Skullcrusher / lying extension
exercises.why: Arms angled back puts the long head partly lengthened; practical pick, not tested directly.

exercises.name: Dips
exercises.why: Heavy compound for triceps and lower chest; no direct trial found.

exercises.name: Back squat (deep)
exercises.why: Squat training grew the quads and adductors more than hip thrusts, and glutes about equally (9-week trial, untrained). Quads tend to grow best at long muscle lengths, so go deep.

exercises.name: Leg press (deep)
exercises.why: Stable way to train the quads through a long range; extrapolated from the range-of-motion review.

exercises.name: Hack squat
exercises.why: Deep, stable quad loading; extrapolated from the range-of-motion review.

exercises.name: Leg extension
exercises.why: Isolation; a 2022 knee-extension study found partials at long muscle lengths grew the quads well. The rectus femoris also gets worked.

exercises.name: Bulgarian split squat
exercises.why: Deep unilateral loading; practical pick when the spine or the gym is the limit.

exercises.name: Seated leg curl
exercises.why: Whole-hamstring volume grew ~14% with seated vs ~9% with prone curls in a 12-week unilateral trial (untrained adults).

exercises.name: Romanian deadlift
exercises.why: Hamstrings loaded while stretched at the hip; same logic as the seated curl, not tested head to head here.

exercises.name: Lying leg curl
exercises.why: The comparator in the study: still grows the hamstrings, just less than seated.

exercises.name: 45° back extension
exercises.why: Practical hip-hinge accessory; no direct trial found.

exercises.name: Barbell hip thrust
exercises.why: Similar glute growth to back squats in a 9-week trial, with higher glute activation. Squats grew thighs more, so thrusts are the glute-only option.

exercises.name: Standing calf raise (full stretch)
exercises.why: Lengthened partial reps gave the largest medial gastroc gain in an 8-week trial in young women, though the margin over full range was unclear. Pause in the stretch.

exercises.name: Seated calf raise
exercises.why: Knee bent shifts work toward the soleus; practical pick, not tested head to head here.

exercises.name: Leg-press calf raise
exercises.why: Easy to load and stretch if you have no standing machine.

exercises.name: Single-leg calf raise off a step
exercises.why: No machine needed; hold a dumbbell to progress.

exercises.name: Conventional deadlift
exercises.why: Heavy full-body pull used in strength training. Heavier loads gave greater 1RM strength gains in a meta-analysis; I found no deadlift-specific growth trial.

exercises.name: Barbell overhead press
exercises.why: Heavy pressing for strength; practical pick, no direct growth trial found.

exercises.name: Barbell row
exercises.why: Heavy horizontal pull for strength; practical pick, no direct growth trial found.

exercises.name: Incline chest press machine
exercises.why: Machine version of an incline press. Machines are stable, so it is easy to train close to failure (common practice, not tested).

exercises.name: Pec deck / chest fly machine
exercises.why: Loads the pec through a long range with the arms out wide; extrapolated from the muscle-length literature, not a chest-specific trial.

exercises.name: Dip machine
exercises.why: Machine dip for triceps and lower chest. Machines are stable, so it is easy to train close to failure (common practice, not tested).

exercises.name: Lateral raise machine
exercises.why: Keeps constant tension on the side delt with no swinging. Machines are stable, so it is easy to train close to failure (common practice, not tested).

exercises.name: Row machine (standing / plate-loaded)
exercises.why: Supported row for the mid-back and lats. Machines are stable, so it is easy to train close to failure (common practice, not tested).

exercises.name: T-bar row
exercises.why: Heavy chest-supported or standing row for the upper back. No direct trial found.

exercises.name: Bicep curl (dumbbell or bar)
exercises.why: The standard curl. Incline and preacher curls load the stretched position more, and that is where the research points.

exercises.name: Pendulum squat
exercises.why: Deep, stable quad loading like the hack squat; extrapolated from the range-of-motion review.
